title: Sequenced Sparkcards: Contextual Checkpoint Walkthrough for New Console Rollouts
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: new users and product teams launching model rollouts in the Redwood Console often miss small but critical steps (telemetry hooks, cost guardrails, canary rules). This increases time-to-first-successful-rollout and drives support tickets and risky misconfigurations.

Proposal: introduce a sequenced set of lightweight "Sparkcards" — micro, anchored UI cards that act as checkpoints in a guided walkthrough for rollout setup and early days post-deploy. Sparkcards are not a full modal tour; they are contextual, dismissible cards with a single micro-action (e.g., enable telemetry, add budget cap, run smoke test, create checkpoint template). Cards appear in sequence: each completed action advances the next card. Progress is visible in the rollout header as simple breadcrumb dots.

Scope: design patterns, copy, visual states, interaction specs, Figma prototype with transitions, analytics event taxonomy, and handoff artifacts for Engineering and PM. Initial surfaces: Rollouts list, Rollout detail (configuration stepper), Cost view quick-check, and Dashboard first-run slot.

Goals: reduce time-to-first-successful-rollout by 30% for new teams in cohort, reduce rollout-related support tickets by 25% in first 90 days, increase telemetry opt-in for rollouts to 75% of new rollouts.

Key UX constraints: minimal disruption to power users, persistent dismiss option, safe defaults for critical toggles, single-action-per-card, keyboard accessible, theming for light/dark, and graceful fallback for private deployments with constrained telemetry.

Deliverables: interaction spec, microcopy deck, Figma prototype (hi-fi + interactive), acceptance criteria checklist, handoff package (components/variants), analytics events list, rollout A/B experiment plan.
acceptance_criteria: Figma prototype demonstrates the full sequence (4–6 cards) with state transitions: initial, completed, skipped, dismissed, reappear logic.
Microcopy approved by PM and legal for telemetry and cost-related language.
Design tokens and component variants documented in the Console component library for card, progress beacon, and dismiss affordance.
Engineering integration hooks specified: analytics events (sparkcard_shown, sparkcard_action, sparkcard_dismiss), and API flag for enabling per-organization spark sequences.
Accessibility review passed (keyboard focus order, aria labels, contrast, screen-reader announcements for state changes).
Canary rollout plan defined with metric targets and rollback criteria.
Handoff notes include telemetry privacy guidance for Private deployments and an opt-out flow for customers with strict data policies.
notes: 2026-02-12: Kickoff with PM + Eng. Agreed on 4-card MVP sequence: enable telemetry, set cost guardrail, create smoke test, apply template.
2026-02-20: Design critique — prefer inline action vs modal. Decision: inline single-action cards to reduce interruption.
2026-02-27: Privacy requested explicit opt-out copy; PM to provide final wording. Action: finalize copy by 2026-03-05.
2026-03-03: Engineering flagged need for per-org feature flag and metrics events. Added to dependencies (ENG-5999).
2026-03-08: Accessibility pre-review — add announcements for completed card transitions and ensure dismiss button tabbable.
2026-03-10: PM review: update target metrics for canary and add support doc link in the final card.
rollout_plan: Canary group: 5% of new orgs for first 2 weeks, monitor metrics: time_to_rollout_completion, telemetry_opt_in_rate, support_ticket_rate.
If telemetry_opt_in_rate < 50% or support_ticket_rate increases >10%, pause and iterate on copy/placement.
Week 3: expand to 25% if canary metrics meet targets; Week 6: full launch with feature flag rollout.
A/B variant: control = no sparkcards; variant A = sequenced sparkcards; variant B = non-sequenced single context card.
qa_checks: Cards appear in correct order and only after prerequisite checks pass (e.g., rollout draft saved).
Analytics events fired with correct payloads and organization IDs redacted for Private deployments.
Dismiss persists across sessions; reappear behavior respects user-level opt-out.
Localization checks for English, French, German, Spanish strings; line-length clipping handled.
Keyboard navigation: tab order, Enter/Space triggers primary action, Escape dismisses card when focused.
Dark mode and high-contrast checked visually and with automated contrast tool.
